title: How to Grill Sliced Kiwi for a Tropical Grilled Fruit Salad
meta_description: Discover how to grill sliced kiwi on a grill mat for a bright tropical fruit salad. Learn step‑by‑step tips, seasoning ideas, and why BBQ Grill Mats are a game‑
html:
Grilling kiwi on a grill mat is a surprisingly easy way to add smoky depth to a fresh tropical fruit salad. The small, delicate slices need a surface that protects them from flare‑ups while still letting the heat caramelize the natural sugars. A reusable non‑stick BBQ Grill Mat does exactly that, giving you perfect grill marks without the fruit sticking or falling through the grates.

Why Use a Grill Mat for Kiwi?

Kiwi’s flesh is soft, and its skin is thin enough that it can easily slip through a standard grill grate. A grill mat creates a flat, even platform that keeps the fruit in place while allowing the heat to circulate. Because the mat is non‑stick, you won’t have to wrestle with pieces that cling to the surface, and you’ll avoid the dreaded flare‑ups that can scorch the fruit.

Choosing the Right Kiwi and Preparing It

Pick ripe but firm kiwis—slight give when you press gently is ideal. Over‑ripe fruit will turn mushy on the grill, while underripe kiwi won’t develop the sweet caramelization you’re after.

  1. Wash the kiwi thoroughly under cold water.
  2. Trim the ends and slice the fruit into ¼‑inch rounds. For a more decorative look, you can cut the rounds into half‑moons.
  3. Pat the slices dry with a paper towel. Moisture on the surface will steam rather than sear.

Once sliced, toss the kiwi lightly with a drizzle of honey or agave and a pinch of sea salt. The sugar helps with caramelization, and the salt amplifies the fruit’s natural flavor.

Setting Up Your Grill and the BBQ Grill Mats

Preheat a gas or charcoal grill to medium‑high (about 375°F–400°F). While the grill is heating, place a BBQ Grill Mat directly on the grates. The mat’s heat‑resistant fibers will handle the temperature without warping.Give the mat a quick spray of high‑heat cooking oil or a light brush of melted butter. Even though the mat is non‑stick, a thin coating helps the kiwi develop a golden crust and makes it easier to transfer the fruit to a serving platter.

Grilling the Kiwi Slices

Lay the kiwi slices in a single layer on the mat, leaving a tiny gap between each piece. Close the grill lid and let the fruit cook for 2–3 minutes. You’ll see gentle grill marks appear and the edges begin to caramelize.

Flip the slices with tongs and grill the other side for another 2 minutes. The fruit should be tender, slightly browned, and still bright green in the center. Remove the kiwi from the mat and set aside while you finish the rest of the salad.

Building the Tropical Grilled Fruit Salad

While the kiwi cools slightly, grill other tropical fruits that benefit from a quick sear—pineapple rings, mango wedges, and banana halves. Use the same BBQ Grill Mats for each fruit to keep the process mess‑free.

  • Arrange the grilled kiwi alongside the other fruits on a large platter.
  • Add a handful of fresh mint leaves and a sprinkle of toasted coconut flakes for crunch.
  • Finish with a drizzle of lime‑honey vinaigrette: whisk together lime juice, honey, a dash of olive oil, and a pinch of chili powder for a subtle heat.

The warm, smoky kiwi pairs beautifully with the bright acidity of the vinaigrette, creating a salad that’s perfect for summer barbecues, brunch buffets, or a light dessert.

Cleaning and Reusing Your Grill Mat

After the grill cools, let the BBQ Grill Mats sit for a few minutes to release any residual grease. Then, hand‑wash them with warm, soapy water and a soft sponge. Avoid abrasive scrubbers; the mat’s surface is designed to stay smooth. Rinse well, shake off excess water, and air‑dry. With proper care, the mat can be reused for dozens of grilling sessions, making it an eco‑friendly alternative to disposable foil.

FAQ

Can I grill other delicate fruits on the same mat?

Absolutely. The non‑stick surface works great for peaches, plums, and even delicate vegetables like asparagus. Just be sure to clean the mat between uses if you’re switching flavor profiles.

Do I need to oil the grill mat for every use?

A light coating of oil or butter each time helps achieve optimal browning and makes the fruit release easily. The mat itself is already non‑stick, so you don’t need a heavy grease layer.

Is a grill mat safe for high‑heat cooking?

Yes. The BBQ Grill Mats are heat‑resistant up to 500°F, which covers typical grilling temperatures for fruits, vegetables, and even meats.
